l4_steps.name: Extract O&D booking history from data lake
l4_steps.input: Daily booking feed from Amadeus Altéa PSS (12-month rolling window)
l4_steps.output: Cleaned O&D demand dataset segmented by cabin, point-of-sale, and booking lead time
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥99%; extraction latency <2 hours from departure day-close
l4_steps.pain_point: Connecting itineraries booked via GDS often log leg-level data only; O&D reconstruction requires custom passenger name record (PNR) stitching logic that breaks during irregular operations

l4_steps.name: Segment O&D demand by fare class and channel
l4_steps.input: Cleaned O&D demand dataset from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Demand segments by fare class (Y/B/M/H/Q/V/W/L/K/G), booking channel, and travel purpose (leisure/business)
l4_steps.kpi: Segment classification accuracy ≥92%; misclassified itineraries <5% of O&D pairs
l4_steps.pain_point: Carriers without seat assignment (open-boarding models) lack seat-map signals for travel-purpose inference, reducing segmentation accuracy vs. assigned-seat competitors

l4_steps.name: Generate 90-day O&D demand forecast
l4_steps.input: Segmented demand history, seasonal indices, special-events calendar
l4_steps.output: 90-day O&D demand forecast by fare class and day-of-week; confidence intervals at 80% and 95%
l4_steps.kpi: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) ≤8% at 60-day horizon; ≤12% at 90-day horizon
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST demand models require minimum 18 months of stable history per O&D; new routes or routes disrupted by major events (e.g., network collapse, weather) cause cold-start forecast degradation

l4_steps.name: Validate forecast against booking pace signals
l4_steps.input: 90-day O&D demand forecast; live booking-curve actuals from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Validated forecast or rework flag with variance root-cause note
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast validation cycle <4 hours; >95% of O&D pairs accepted without manual override
l4_steps.pain_point: Sudden demand spikes driven by flash sales or competitor capacity withdrawal are not captured by statistical models, requiring analyst intervention outside automated tolerance bands

l4_steps.name: Calculate network contribution per itinerary
l4_steps.input: Validated O&D demand forecast; filed fare inventory from ATPCO; connection rules from Amadeus Altéa
l4_steps.output: O&D contribution matrix: revenue yield, spill cost, and recapture probability per itinerary
l4_steps.kpi: Network revenue contribution accuracy within ±3% of post-departure actuals; matrix refresh latency ≤6 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Point-to-point network topology limits connecting itinerary combinations available for O&D value netting; contribution calculation must account for high-frequency same-city multi-flight options

l4_steps.name: Benchmark competitive fares by O&D market
l4_steps.input: Competitor schedule data (OAG), ATPCO published fares, Sabre GDS fare feeds
l4_steps.output: Competitive gap analysis: own-fare vs. lowest available competitor fare by O&D and booking lead time
l4_steps.kpi: Competitive fare index maintained within ±5% of market median for top-50 revenue O&D pairs
l4_steps.pain_point: Competitor dynamic pricing and NDC fare products are not consistently visible through ATPCO filings; private corporate fares and carrier-direct channel fares create persistent blind spots in competitive benchmarking

l4_steps.name: Assess O&D contribution validity
l4_steps.input: O&D contribution matrix; competitive gap analysis
l4_steps.output: Approved contribution matrix or rework instruction with adjustment rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Gate review cycle ≤2 hours; <10% of O&D pairs requiring manual contribution override
l4_steps.pain_point: High-frequency thin markets (routes with <5 flights/week) produce contribution estimates with wide confidence intervals; analysts must apply manual floors to prevent bid price collapse on low-frequency O&Ds

l4_steps.name: Run LP network optimisation for bid prices
l4_steps.input: Approved O&D contribution matrix; 90-day demand forecast; current flight leg capacities from Altéa
l4_steps.output: Shadow prices (bid prices) per leg-class combination for each active departure window
l4_steps.kpi: Optimisation solve time ≤45 minutes for full network; bid price solution feasibility ≥99.5% of legs
l4_steps.pain_point: LP model size grows quadratically with O&D pairs; large banks of short-haul turns can exceed solver memory limits, requiring network partitioning that degrades optimality

l4_steps.name: Review bid price reasonableness
l4_steps.input: Generated bid prices; prior-day bid prices; yield targets by O&D
l4_steps.output: Validated bid prices or escalation to RM Manager with variance explanation
l4_steps.kpi: Bid price variance vs. prior day flagged if >20%; analyst review cycle ≤90 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Automated bid prices occasionally produce outliers on O&Ds with thin history or solver anomalies; without mandatory review thresholds, outlier prices can suppress availability on high-demand markets

l4_steps.name: Publish approved bid prices to inventory
l4_steps.output: Bid prices committed to Altéa PSS availability engine; audit log entry with timestamp and analyst sign-off
l4_steps.kpi: Bid price publication latency <15 minutes from approval; 100% of active departures covered within the 90-day window
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa availability cache refresh is asynchronous; published bid prices may not be visible to GDS availability queries for up to 10 minutes, creating a transient window where under-priced availability is sold

l4_steps.name: Apply O&D class controls to Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Published bid prices; authorisation levels (AU) per fare class from NRM
l4_steps.output: Updated fare class open/close status in Altéa inventory; availability snapshot distributed to GDS and NDC channels
l4_steps.kpi: Class control accuracy ≥99.8% (no misapplied open/close); distribution sync to all GDS channels <5 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa virtual class nesting requires correct AU configuration per booking class; misconfigured inheritance rules cause availability bleed-through where higher-value classes sell below bid price

l4_steps.name: Monitor intraday booking pace vs. forecast
l4_steps.input: Real-time bookings from Altéa PSS; validated O&D demand forecast
l4_steps.output: Intraday booking pace report; pace-vs-forecast variance by O&D and fare class
l4_steps.kpi: Monitoring refresh interval ≤30 minutes; pace deviation alerts triggered at ±10% threshold
l4_steps.pain_point: Bulk GDS batch bookings (travel agency group uploads) cause instantaneous pace spikes that trigger false-positive alerts; lack of booking intent signals before ticketing makes proactive controls difficult

l4_steps.name: Evaluate booking pace deviation trigger
l4_steps.input: Intraday pace report; alert flags for O&Ds exceeding ±10% deviation
l4_steps.output: Decision: hold current controls, tighten availability, or open additional classes
l4_steps.kpi: Override response time <60 minutes from alert; revenue impact of late override <0.5% of flight revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: Intraday override authority is often limited to Senior Analysts; escalation to RM Manager during off-hours (night departures, weekend shifts) delays response and allows continued mis-pricing

l4_steps.name: Execute manual availability override
l4_steps.input: Override instruction (tighten or open classes); fare class control screen in Altéa
l4_steps.output: Revised class availability posted to Altéa; override action logged with business justification
l4_steps.kpi: Override-to-publish latency <10 minutes; 100% of overrides logged with analyst ID and rationale
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual override in Altéa bypasses NRM optimisation logic; overrides that remain in place beyond the intended window lock in suboptimal availability and are difficult to detect without dedicated override-expiry workflow

l4_steps.name: Capture post-departure O&D revenue actuals
l4_steps.input: Final departure manifest from Altéa; ticketing revenue records from BSP / ARC settlement
l4_steps.output: Post-departure O&D revenue report: RASM, yield, load factor, spill, and spoilage by fare class
l4_steps.kpi: Report availability ≤24 hours post-departure; O&D revenue reconciliation variance vs. settlement <0.2%
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP/ARC settlement files arrive 48–72 hours post-departure; provisional revenue figures used in day-1 reporting may differ materially from final settled amounts, inflating apparent yield performance

l4_steps.name: Evaluate demand model accuracy
l4_steps.output: Model accuracy scorecard (MAPE by O&D, phase, and departure horizon); recalibration flag if accuracy <85%
l4_steps.kpi: Model accuracy review completed within 5 business days of departure; ≥85% of O&D pairs meeting MAPE target
l4_steps.pain_point: Forecast accuracy degrades systematically for new O&Ds, seasonal routes restarted after winter suspension, and markets affected by competitor schedule changes — all require manual baseline resets that the NRM auto-calibration does not trigger

l4_steps.name: Recalibrate O&D demand models
l4_steps.input: Recalibration flag; post-departure actuals; external demand signals (GDP, events, competitor changes)
l4_steps.output: Updated model parameters committed to NRM; change log with effective date and recalibration rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Recalibration turnaround ≤3 business days; post-recalibration MAPE improvement ≥15% on flagged O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM model recalibration requires analyst SQL access to Redshift parameter tables; access provisioning delays during analyst onboarding leave new team members unable to execute recalibrations independently
